**[t1] Chris (facilitator):** Hello Mei. What is the central frustration you experience when managing multi-currency household finances?

**[t2] Mei (stakeholder):** My partner and I earn income in Singapore dollars and British pounds. We need our family budget to consolidate multiple currency accounts into a unified monthly expenditure view.

**[t3] Chris (facilitator):** How do you currently handle money transfers across those accounts?

**[t4] Mei (stakeholder):** We send remittances every month into our cross-border family savings wallet. It is crucial to track when those funds convert so exchange rate swings do not distort our savings targets.

**[t5] Chris (facilitator):** Does the system need to track currency fluctuations in that account daily?

**[t6] Mei (stakeholder):** Yes, that secondary account needs daily exchange valuation updates so we see the true purchasing power of our joint savings.

**[t7] Chris (facilitator):** How do retail banking transaction charges affect your household balance?

**[t8] Mei (stakeholder):** Ugh, don't get me started on retail banks. Traditional banks rob ordinary families with absurd three-percent hidden markups on foreign transfers and twenty-dollar wire fees. It is completely outrageous predatory behavior.

**[t9] Chris (facilitator):** That fee transparency pain is very clear. What about categorizing daily grocery and dining receipts?

**[t10] Mei (stakeholder):** Household members should be able to categorize shared living expenses so both partners understand where the money went.

**[t11] Chris (facilitator):** How should users feel when opening the application after a high-spending weekend?

**[t12] Mei (stakeholder):** Reviewing monthly expenses should feel encouraging and calm rather than triggering financial guilt or panic.

**[t13] Chris (facilitator):** Should the app give recommendations on wealth investments or stock trading?

**[t14] Chris (facilitator):** Could it recommend mutual funds or algorithmic equity trades?

**[t15] Chris (facilitator):** What is the boundary on automated financial guidance?

**[t16] Mei (stakeholder):** To be completely clear, we are definitely not building an automated stock trading bot or robo-advisor that executes transactions, because that introduces massive financial risk.

**[t17] Chris (facilitator):** That is a very clean negative boundary. How should future savings targets be modeled?

**[t18] Mei (stakeholder):** We want to track progress toward long-term family savings goals across different currencies without manual recalculation.

**[t19] Chris (facilitator):** Are cash receipts also included in the tracking?

**[t20] Mei (stakeholder):** Yes, users should be able to log manual cash transactions quickly when overseas travel prevents card payments.
